content: 1. French MD et al. conducted a study on the school-based control of urinary schistosomiasis in Zanzibar, Tanzania. They monitored micro-haematuria using reagent strips as a rapid urological assessment tool. This study was published in the Journal of Pediatric Urology in 2007. 2. Massa K et al. explored community perceptions regarding community-directed treatment and school-based approaches for controlling schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminthiasis among school-age children in Lushoto District, Tanzania. Their findings were published in the Journal of Biosocial Science in 2009. 3. Massa K et al. compared the effects of community-directed treatment versus school-based treatment approaches on the prevalence and intensity of schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminthiasis among schoolchildren in Tanzania. This research was published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2009. 4. Brooker S, Clements AC, and Bundy DAP reviewed the global epidemiology, ecology, and control of soil-transmitted helminth infections. Their systematic review was published in Advances in Parasitology in 2006. 5. Mohammed KA et al. conducted a safety study on the triple co-administration of ivermectin, albendazole, and praziquantel in Zanzibar. Their findings were published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2008. 6. Olsen A reviewed the efficacy and safety of drug combinations in treating schistosomiasis, soil-transmitted helminthiasis, lymphatic filariasis, and onchocerciasis. This review was published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2007. 7. Bundy DA et al. discussed the relationship between deworming and development, emphasizing the importance of asking the right questions. Their work was published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2009. 8. Smits HL examined the prospects for controlling neglected tropical diseases through mass drug administration. This analysis was published in the Expert Review of Anti-infective Therapy in 2009. 9. Churcher TS et al. identified sub-optimal responses to ivermectin in the treatment of river blindness. Their findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America in 2009. 10. Churcher TS and Basáñez MG discussed sampling strategies to detect anthelmintic resistance in human onchocerciasis. Their study was published in Trends in Parasitology in 2009. 11. Mathieu E et al. compared methods for estimating drug coverage for filariasis elimination in Leogane Commune, Haiti. Their findings were published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2003. 12. Geary TG et al. highlighted unresolved issues in anthelmintic pharmacology for human helminthiases. Their review was published in the International Journal for Parasitology in 2010. 13. Ramaiah KD reviewed the progress and challenges of the lymphatic filariasis elimination program in India. This review was published in Trends in Parasitology in 2009. 14. Wanjii S et al. studied the community-directed delivery of doxycycline for treating onchocerciasis in areas co-endemic with loiasis in Cameroon. Their findings were published in Parasites & Vectors in 2009. 15. Diawara A et al. developed assays to detect beta-tubulin codon 200 polymorphism in Trichuris trichiura and Ascaris lumbricoides. Their study was published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2009. 16. McManus DP and Loukas A reviewed the current status of vaccines for schistosomiasis. Their review was published in Clinical Microbiology Reviews in 2008. 17. Doenhoff MJ et al. discussed chemotherapy and drug resistance in schistosomiasis, fascioliasis, and tapeworm infections. This chapter was included in the book Antimicrobial Drug Resistance edited by DL Mayers in 2009. 18. Lightowlers MW reviewed vaccination strategies for preventing cysticercosis. This review was published in Developments in Biologicals in 2004. 19. Keiser J and Utzinger J conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of current drugs against soil-transmitted helminth infections. Their findings were published in the Journal of the American Medical Association in 2008. 20. Stepek G et al. questioned whether new control methods are required for human gastrointestinal nematode infections. Their study was published in the International Journal of Experimental Pathology in 2006. 21. Hu Y, Xiao SH, and Aroian RV identified tribendimidine as an L-type nicotinic acetylcholine receptor agonist. Their findings were published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2009. 22. Wolstenholme AJ et al. reviewed drug resistance in veterinary helminths. Their review was published in Trends in Parasitology in 2004. 23. Martin PJ, Anderson N, and Jarrett RG evaluated methods for detecting benzimidazole resistance using fecal egg count reduction tests and in vitro assays. Their study was published in the Australian Veterinary Journal in 1989. 24. De Clercq D et al. reported the failure of mebendazole in treating human hookworm infections in southern Mali. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1997. 25. Sacko M et al. compared the efficacy of mebendazole, albendazole, and pyrantel in treating human hookworm infections in southern Mali. Their study was published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1999. 26. Reynolds JA et al. reported the failure of pyrantel in treating human hookworm infections in northwest Australia. Their findings were published in Acta Tropica in 1997. 27. Albonico M et al. evaluated the efficacy of mebendazole and levamisole, alone or in combination, against intestinal nematode infections in Zanzibar. Their study was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2003. 28. Flohr C et al. reported low efficacy of mebendazole against hookworm in Vietnam through two randomized controlled trials. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2007. 29. Albonico M, Wright V, and Bickle Q conducted molecular analysis of the beta-tubulin gene in human hookworms to investigate potential benzimidazole resistance on Pemba Island. Their study was published in Molecular and Biochemical Parasitology in 2004. 30. Schwenkenbecher JM et al. characterized beta-tubulin genes in hookworms and investigated resistance-associated mutations using real-time PCR. Their findings were published in Molecular and Biochemical Parasitology in 2007.
